title: How long is the projection of a tilted rod?
description: A rod thirteen centimetres long is held above a table with one end five centimetres higher than the other. The board finds the projection with the right triangle rule and then asks when the projection would equal the rod. Keeko's doubt is that the projection is eight centimetres.
teaching_notes: One idea: the rod, its projection and the height gap form a right triangle with the rod as the longest side, so the projection is shorter than the rod unless the gap is zero. Watch for students who subtract the lengths instead of the squares.

source: A rod 13 cm long is held above a table so that one end is 5
video_script.why: The child finds the projection of a tilted rod with the right triangle rule and sees when it equals the rod, because the projection is shorter than the rod unless the gap is zero.
video_script.substitution: rod 13 cm; height gap 5 cm; projection squared = 13 x 13 - 5 x 5 = 169 - 25 = 144; projection = square root of 144 = 12 cm; with a gap of 0 the projection is 13 cm.
video_script.anchor: the rod above the table with both ends dropped straight down, forming a right triangle
video_script.wrong_answer: the rod is thirteen and the gap is five, so the projection is eight centimetres
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes 13 - 5 = 8 cm; the gap stands upright and the projection lies flat, at a right angle, so the squares take away: 169 - 25 = 144 and the projection is 12 cm, which strikes the doubt.
video_script.payoff_line: The projection is twelve centimetres, and thirteen only with the rod parallel to the table

final_answer.value: 12 cm; it would be 13 cm only with the rod parallel to the table
final_answer.spoken: twelve centimetres; it would be thirteen centimetres only with the rod parallel to the table

names.Ziva: the theorem used for the shortest path of 40 cm

hold_back: 12 cm; it would be 13 cm only with the rod parallel to the table
maths_rules: the projection of an object is made by dropping every place of it straight down onto the plane, at a right angle
the rod, its projection and the height gap make a right triangle; the rod is the longest side
square of the longest side = sum of the squares of the other two
the projection equals 13 cm only when the gap is 0, that is, when the rod is parallel to the table
wrong idea: 13 - 5 = 8 takes away the lengths; at a right angle the squares take away
video_script.design: One idea: the rod, its projection and the gap make a right triangle. The rod is held above the table on the stage; both ends drop straight down, and the triangle is drawn in the accent colour.

beats.on_screen: To find: the length of the projection; when it would be 13 cm

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the projection, and when it would be thirteen centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: right triangle: longest side = rod = 13 cm; upright side = height gap = 5 cm; flat side = projection

marks.long: the rod is marked as the longest side, 13 cm
marks.gap: the height gap is marked as the upright side, 5 cm
marks.flat: the projection is marked as the flat side

narration: <bookmark mark='long'/>Step one, name the sides of the right triangle. The rod is the longest side, thirteen centimetres.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>The height gap is the upright side, five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='flat'/>The projection is the flat side that we want.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: square of the longest side = sum of the squares of the other two; projection squared = 13 x 13 - 5 x 5

marks.rule: the rule: square of the longest side = sum of the squares of the other two
marks.rewrite: the rule is rewritten as projection squared = 13 x 13 - 5 x 5

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, the Ziva Theorem is about right triangles. It says the square of the longest side is the sum of the squares of the other two.
<bookmark mark='rewrite'/>Here, the square of the projection is the square of thirteen, take away the square of five.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: projection squared = 13 x 13 - 5 x 5 = 169 - 25 = 144; projection = square root of 144 = 12 cm

marks.sq: the squares 169 and 25 are written one under the other
marks.root: the words projection = square root of 144 = 12 cm are written

narration: <bookmark mark='sq'/>Step three, thirteen times thirteen is one hundred and sixty nine, and five times five is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='take'/>One hundred and sixty nine take away twenty five is one hundred and forty four.
<bookmark mark='root'/>The square root of one hundred and forty four is twelve. The projection is twelve centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: if the height gap is 0, the projection squared = 13 x 13, so the projection is 13 cm

marks.lower: the raised end of the rod comes down until the height gap is 0
marks.same: the projection grows to the full length of the rod

narration: <bookmark mark='lower'/>Step four, bring the raised end down until the height gap is zero.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Then nothing is taken away, and the projection is as long as the rod.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 12 cm; it would be 13 cm only with the rod parallel to the table
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The projection is twelve centimetres, and thirteen only with the rod parallel to the table.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the rod is thirteen and the gap is five, so the projection is eight centimetres.
<bookmark mark='angle'/>The gap stands upright and the projection lies flat, at a right angle.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Sides at a right angle do not take away like that. Their squares do.
